overview: Both are antigen-presenting cells that engulf pathogens, but dendritic cells specialise in kicking off the adaptive immune response.
genZNote: Macrophages: the general clean-up-and-eat crew. Dendritic cells: the specialist that grabs evidence and rushes it to headquarters (the lymph node).

aspects.label: Primary Role
aspects.valueA: The most effective and dedicated antigen-presenting cell, specialised for activating naive T cells.
aspects.valueB: General-purpose phagocyte, mainly focused on engulfing and digesting pathogens/debris.

aspects.label: Typical Location
aspects.valueA: Found in tissues exposed to the environment (skin, mucosa), then migrates to lymph nodes to present antigen.
aspects.valueB: Distributed throughout tissues and blood, staying mostly local to clear pathogens/debris.

aspects.label: Efficiency at Activating Naive T Cells
aspects.valueA: Highly efficient — considered the primary initiator of adaptive immune responses.
aspects.valueB: Can present antigen, but far less efficient than dendritic cells at activating naive T cells.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Dendritic cells are often called the 'sentinels' of the immune system because they are the main bridge between innate and adaptive immunity.
overlay.memoryTrick: Dendritic cells alert headquarters (lymph nodes). Macrophages mostly clean up on-site.
overlay.commonMisconception: Macrophages are not useless for activating T cells — they simply aren't the primary initiators; dendritic cells hold that specialised role.
